subtopics.title: IQAir report 2025: scope and compliance
subtopics.summary: The 8th World Air Quality Report 2025 was released by Swiss IQAir, which assesses air quality using PM2.5 concentrations. IQAir's coverage grew from 134 countries in 2023 to 143 countries and 9,446 cities in 2025. Only 14% of cities met the WHO PM2.5 annual guideline in 2025, down from 17% in 2024.
facts: Report: 8th World Air Quality Report 2025, by Swiss IQAir
IQAir assessments are based on PM2.5 (fine particulate matter) concentrations
Coverage: 134 countries in 2023, then 143 countries and 9,446 cities in 2025
Only 14% of cities complied with the WHO PM2.5 annual guideline in 2025
City compliance share declined from 17% in 2024
Only 13 countries/territories met the WHO PM2.5 guidelines
130 of 143 countries and territories failed to meet safe air quality standards
Nieuwoudtville (South Africa) recorded as World's Cleanest City, PM2.5 level 1.0 µg/m³
IQAir is a Swiss air quality technology company founded in 1963, HQ in Goldach, Switzerland

subtopics.title: Most polluted countries, cities and regions
subtopics.summary: Pakistan was the most polluted country in 2025, with PM2.5 levels over 13 times the WHO limit. Loni in Uttar Pradesh was the most polluted city, about 22 times above WHO guidelines. Five of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India, and Central and South Asia remain the most polluted regions globally.
facts: Most polluted country in 2025: Pakistan, PM2.5 at 67.3 µg/m³
Pakistan's PM2.5 level is over 13 times the WHO limit
Pakistan was followed by Bangladesh, Tajikistan, Chad and Democratic Republic of Congo
Most polluted city: Loni, Uttar Pradesh, about 22 times WHO guidelines
5 of the world's 10 most polluted cities are in India: Loni, Byrnihat, Delhi, Ghaziabad, Ula
India ranked 6th most polluted country in 2025 (5th in 2024)
New Delhi is the world's most polluted capital for 8 consecutive years
India accounted for 74 of the world's 100 most polluted cities in 2024
Central and South Asia remain the most polluted regions globally

subtopics.title: National framework and monitoring tools in India
subtopics.summary: India's National Air Quality Index, launched in 2014, explains pollution in simple categories. The Graded Response Action Plan is an emergency measure that applies only when air quality shifts from Poor to Very Poor, and the Supreme Court approved it in 2016. The National Clean Air Programme, launched in 2019, targets a 40% cut in average particulate matter by 2026 in 131 cities.
facts: National Air Quality Index (2014) communicates air quality in easy terms; launched by Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)
AQI categories: Good, Satisfactory, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor, Severe
GRAP (2017): emergency measures that kick in only when air quality shifts from Poor to Very Poor
GRAP was submitted by CPCB and approved by the Supreme Court in 2016 (MC Mehta vs Union of India)
GRAP is implemented by the Commission for Air Quality Management
National Clean Air Programme launched in 2019 by the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change
NCAP goal: 40% reduction in average particulate matter concentrations by 2026 in 131 cities
The 131 non-attainment cities under NCAP were identified by CPCB
PRANA portal launched to track NCAP progress and regulate air pollution in non-attainment cities
SAFAR is a Ministry of Earth Sciences initiative for city-wide and localised air quality monitoring

subtopics.title: Vehicle, fuel, farm and legal measures
subtopics.summary: Vehicle norms, clean-fuel schemes and farm tools target different sources of pollution. Bharat Stage VI became mandatory nationwide in 2020, while FAME promotes electric and hybrid vehicles. Legal protection includes the Fundamental Duty in Article 51A(g), added in 1976, and the reading of Article 21 to cover a healthy environment.
facts: Bharat Stage VI (2020): mandatory leap from BS-IV to BS-VI, implemented nationwide
FAME scheme promotes adoption of electric and hybrid vehicles
Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provides LPG as clean cooking fuel, reducing biomass-based cooking
SATAT initiative promotes compressed bio-gas to manage agricultural waste
GRIHA encourages sustainable, eco-friendly practices in building construction and operation
Turbo Happy Seeder uproots stubble and sows seeds in the cleared area
Pusa Bio-Decomposer turns crop residue into manure in 15-20 days; developed by Indian Agricultural Research Institute
42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Clause (g) in Article 51A: protecting and improving the natural environment is a Fundamental Duty
Article 21 interpreted to include the right to a healthy environment
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981; Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974; Environment Protection Act, 1986

quizzes.title: Global findings check
quizzes.passage: Air quality around the world is often measured by the concentration of fine particulate matter, known as PM2.5, because these tiny particles can travel deep into the lungs. Health agencies set a guideline for the annual average level of these particles, and a global assessment checks how many places meet it. The assessment discussed here is prepared by a technology company that measures air quality and reports the results. Its coverage has grown over time, and the latest edition includes far more countries and cities than the earlier one did. Every reading is compared against the same guideline, so results from very different places can be placed side by side on one scale. Wider coverage matters because a place without monitors can look clean on paper while its residents breathe polluted air, and an honest comparison needs data from many locations. The findings are sobering. Only a small share of cities met the annual guideline in the latest year, and that share fell from the previous year. Most of the countries and territories assessed did not meet safe air quality standards. Only a handful of places met the guideline, and at least one city recorded very low particle levels, which shows that clean air is still possible.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the World Air Quality Report 2025:
I. 130 of 143 countries and territories failed to meet safe air quality standards.
II. Central and South Asia remain the most polluted regions globally.
III. Five of the world's ten most polluted cities are located in Pakistan.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the report, while III is wrong because five of the ten most polluted cities are in India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India in the World Air Quality Report 2025:
I. India was ranked the 6th most polluted country in 2025.
II. India's ranking improved from 5th in 2024.
III. India accounted for 50 of the world's 100 most polluted cities in 2024.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because India accounted for 74 of the top 100 cities in 2024.

quizzes.title: India's framework check
quizzes.passage: India manages air pollution through several tools that work at different stages. The first is a public information tool, a national index that converts complex pollution readings into simple categories from good to severe, so that citizens can understand the air they breathe. The second is an emergency framework. Its measures are triggered only when air quality worsens from one stage to a more dangerous one, and their purpose is to prevent further deterioration. The Supreme Court approved this emergency framework in a case concerning the environment. The third is a long-term national programme. It asks cities identified as non-attainment to reduce average particulate levels within a fixed period, and an online portal supports the tracking of its progress. The fourth is a monitoring initiative run by a government ministry, which provides city-wide and localised air quality information for major metropolitan areas and also issues weather forecasts and research. Each tool serves a different purpose, and none of them works alone. Public categories help people judge how careful to be on bad days, while emergency steps are reserved for the most severe deterioration. Long-term programmes address pollution that persists over many months and years, and monitoring tells authorities where action is needed. Together, these tools link public information, emergency response and long-term planning.

questions.q: Which central body launched the National Air Quality Index in 2014?
questions.explanation: The National Air Quality Index was launched in 2014 by the Central Pollution Control Board.

questions.q: In which year did the Supreme Court approve the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP)?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court approved GRAP in its 2016 verdict in MC Mehta vs Union of India.

questions.q: In which year was the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) launched?
questions.explanation: The National Clean Air Programme was launched in 2019 by the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change.

questions.q: How many non-attainment cities does the National Clean Air Programme cover? (give a number)
questions.explanation: NCAP covers 131 non-attainment cities identified by the Central Pollution Control Board.

questions.q: What is the targeted reduction in average particulate matter concentrations under NCAP by 2026, in per cent?
questions.explanation: NCAP aims to reduce average particulate matter concentrations by 40% by 2026.

questions.q: Which ministry runs SAFAR, the city-wide air quality monitoring initiative?
questions.explanation: SAFAR is a Ministry of Earth Sciences initiative to monitor city-wide and localised air quality.

questions.q: Which portal was launched to track NCAP progress and regulate air pollution in non-attainment cities?
accept: Portal for Regulation of Air-Pollution in Non-Attainment Cities
